sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空的七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的外面是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一个锅的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝175周年，帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受特惠，网址为nytimes.com斜杠subscribe。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。ぴ

sentences.en: Over the past few weeks, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几周里，美国

sentences.en: stock market has been on a tear, soaring to record levels and delivering a shot in the arm to retirement accounts.
sentences.zh: 股市一路飙升，创下历史新高，给退休账户打了一剂强心针。

sentences.en: The trouble is, millions of Americans don't have such accounts, and even if they do, have little or no money inside of them.
sentences.zh: 问题是，数百万美国人根本没有这样的账户，即使有，里面也几乎没有钱。

sentences.en: My colleague, Michael Steinberger, has been trying to figure out why Americans are retiring so poorly and traces much of it back to our growing reliance on the 401k.
sentences.zh: 我的同事迈克尔·斯坦伯格一直在试图弄清楚为什么美国人的退休生活如此糟糕，并将很大一部分原因追溯到我们对401(k)日益增长的依赖。

sentences.en: It's Monday, May 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月20日，星期一。

sentences.en: Michael, we are going to talk to you today about what doesn't look on paper like the world's sexiest subject, but I think actually is a very sexy subject,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我们今天要和你聊一个在纸面上看起来不像是世界上最性感的话题，但我认为它实际上是一个非常性感的话题，

sentences.en: which is retirement in the United States.
sentences.zh: 那就是美国的退休问题。

sentences.en: And you began your journalistic inquiry into the subject of retirement in America with a very provocative question.
sentences.zh: 你带着一个非常具有挑衅性的问题，开始了你对美国退休制度的新闻调查。

sentences.en: You asked, was the 401k a mistake?
sentences.zh: 你问，401(k)是一个错误吗？

sentences.en: Has this vast system of personal retirement plans that we now all rely on, pretty much, has it failed us?
sentences.zh: 我们现在几乎所有人都在依赖的这个庞大的个人退休计划系统，它是不是失败了？

sentences.en: And I wonder why exactly you decided to ask that provocative question right now.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你究竟为什么决定在这个时候提出这个挑衅性的问题？

sentences.en: I ask that question right now because we are having an unprecedented number of Americans reaching retirement age.
sentences.zh: 我之所以在这个时候提出这个问题，是因为有史以来数量空前的美国人正在到达退休年龄。

sentences.en: This year alone, it's estimated that 4.1 million Americans will turn 65.
sentences.zh: 仅今年一年，预计就有410万美国人将年满65岁。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's a record number, what the AARP calls the silver tsunami.
sentences.zh: 这是一个创纪录的数字，被AARP（美国退休人员协会）称为“白银海啸”。

sentences.en: And this is the first cohort of Americans, the first generation of Americans who entered the workforce 40 years ago when 401ks became sort of the dominant vehicle
sentences.zh: 这是第一批美国人，第一代美国人，他们在40年前进入职场，当时401(k)成为了某种主导工具

sentences.en: for establishing a retirement nest egg.
sentences.zh: 用于建立退休金储蓄。

sentences.en: 401ks, just for the sake of clarity, our employer-provided retirement savings plans.
sentences.zh: 为了清晰起见，401(k)是我们雇主提供的退休储蓄计划。

sentences.en: Basically, you set aside a certain portion of your paycheck to an investment account of your choosing.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你把工资的一部分存入你选择的投资账户中。

sentences.en: And the hope is that those contributions, with the help of the financial markets, will grow substantially over time.
sentences.zh: 希望这些缴款在金融市场的帮助下，随着时间的推移会有大幅增长。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so this generation of American workers that's now entering retirement age are the products of a 40-year experiment with self-directed retirement financing.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在进入退休年龄的这代美国工人，是历时40年的自主导退休融资实验的产物。

sentences.en: And now we get to see whether it worked.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来看看它是否奏效。

sentences.en: And we know it worked well for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它对很多人来说运作良好。

sentences.en: The concern is that it didn't work as well for many others.
sentences.zh: 令人担忧的是，对许多其他人来说，它并没有那么好。

sentences.en: And that a lot of Americans are now reaching retirement age without having adequate money put aside for their retirements.
sentences.zh: 许多美国人现在到达退休年龄时，却没有为退休存够足够的钱。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Just how inadequate is that retirement picture?
sentences.zh: 那幅退休图景究竟有多不充足？

sentences.en: One estimate is that 49% of people in the 55 to 65 age bracket have nothing put aside for retirement.
sentences.zh: 一项估计是，55至65岁年龄段的人中有49%的人没有为退休存下任何东西。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The numbers are quite stark.
sentences.zh: 这些数字相当严峻。

sentences.en: Half of the population of those at or near retirement have nothing put away.
sentences.zh: 达到或接近退休年龄的人口中有的一半没有任何积蓄。

sentences.en: That's what the numbers indicate.
sentences.zh: 这就是数字所表明的。

sentences.en: And depending on the estimate, we're looking at maybe 10 to 20% of all seniors already are living in poverty.
sentences.zh: 根据不同的估计，我们看到大约10%到20%的老年人已经生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: And so for many, retirement is an unobtainable aspiration.
sentences.zh: 因此，对许多人来说，退休是一个无法企及的愿望。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And there's a strong case to be made that 401ks are largely responsible for the fact that so many Americans don't have adequate savings.
sentences.zh: 有强有力的理由表明，401(k)在很大程度上导致了如此多的美国人没有足够的积蓄。

sentences.en: Well, this feels like the moment in a daily episode where I think we have to roll back the tape a bit and have you explain how this 40-year-old 401k experiment ever began.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这感觉就像是每日播客节目里的那个时刻，我想我们得把磁带倒回一点，让你解释一下这个有40年历史的401(k)实验是怎么开始的。

sentences.en: So let's start with the story of how we have come to rely so much on the 401k in the first place.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们从我们如何变得如此依赖401(k)的故事开始。

sentences.en: Well, I think it would be good to start that story with the system that existed before 401ks came along.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为用401(k)出现之前存在的系统来开始这个故事会很好。

sentences.en: Back in the 50s, 60s, and into the 70s, a lot of companies offered their workers pensions.
sentences.zh: 早在50年代、60年代和70年代，许多公司都为他们的工人提供养老金。

sentences.en: And pensions were basically the company would create a pool of assets.
sentences.zh: 养老金基本上就是公司建立一个资产池。

sentences.en: It would manage the money, invest the money, and manage it on behalf of employees.
sentences.zh: 它管理资金，投资资金，并代表员工进行管理。

sentences.en: And if you worked for a company long enough, you were guaranteed a fixed retirement income provided by the company for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一家公司工作的时间足够长，你就能保证获得由公司提供的、余生固定的退休收入。

sentences.en: Right, and the key word there is guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 对，这里的关键词是“保证”。

sentences.en: Companies guaranteed that your pension would be at a certain level, essentially in perpetuity.
sentences.zh: 公司保证你的养老金会在一定水平上，基本上是永久的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you worked for a major steel or auto company and you spent 30 years,
sentences.zh: 如果你在一家大型钢铁或汽车公司工作，你花 了30年，

sentences.en: 40 years working on the assembly line of that company, you knew that when you retired, you were going to be getting a fixed monthly income from the company,
sentences.zh: 40年在该公司的装配线上工作，你知道当你退休时，你将从公司获得固定的月收入，

sentences.en: you knew what the amount would be.
sentences.zh: 你知道金额会是多少。

sentences.en: And it was a huge benefit to working for these companies.
sentences.zh: 为这些公司工作是一个巨大的福利。

sentences.en: It was a different era, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一个不同的时代。

sentences.en: There was an era of lifetime employment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个终身雇佣的时代。

sentences.en: People often spent their entire careers with the same company.
sentences.zh: 人们通常在同一家公司度过他们的整个职业生涯。

sentences.en: And people also didn't live as long.
sentences.zh: 而且人们也没有活那么久。

sentences.en: From a company's point of view, pensions were affordable.
sentences.zh: 从公司的角度来看，养老金是负担得起的。

sentences.en: And it was just a very different time.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个非常不同的时代。

sentences.en: And it should be said that even in the heyday of pensions, only around half of all private sector workers had them.
sentences.zh: 必须指出的是，即使在养老金的鼎盛时期，也只有大约一半的私营部门工人拥有养老金。

sentences.en: So they weren't as broad-based as people might think.
sentences.zh: 所以它们并没有人们想象的那么广泛。

sentences.en: And these days, there's a bit of mythologizing about that era.
sentences.zh: 而现在，对那个时代有一点神话色彩。

sentences.en: But if you had one, it was something you cherished.
sentences.zh: 但是如果你有一个，那是你倍加珍惜的东西。

sentences.en: And it was an era in which the country seemed to do a better job of taking care of the working person.
sentences.zh: 那是一个国家在照顾劳动人民方面似乎做得更好的时代。

sentences.en: Well, then who would willingly give up that cherished system of the pension?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁会自愿放弃那个备受珍视的养老金系统呢？

sentences.en: Well, 401ks came along as almost a historical accident.
sentences.zh: 嗯，401(k)的出现几乎是一个历史偶然。

sentences.en: In the 60s and 70s, many companies were looking for ways to reward their executives.
sentences.zh: 在60年代和70年代，许多公司都在寻找奖励高管的方法。

sentences.en: And specifically, they were looking for ways that they could award bonuses to executives and not have that money taxed.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他们正在寻找可以向高管颁发奖金且这笔钱不被征税的方法。

sentences.en: The top marginal tax rate at the time was quite high.
sentences.zh: 当时最高边际税率相当高。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so some companies began offering tax-deferred savings plans to executives to help them minimize their tax hit.
sentences.zh: 因此，一些公司开始向高管提供税收递延储蓄计划，以帮助他们将税收冲击降到最低。

sentences.en: Basically, the way these worked was that the company would pay bonuses directly into these accounts and the executives could only take the money out when they left the company,
sentences.zh: 基本上，这些计划的工作方式是公司将奖金直接支付到这些账户中，高管只有在离开公司时才能把钱取出来，

sentences.en: either take out of the job or to retire.
sentences.zh: 无论是离职还是退休。

sentences.en: But there was always a certain murkiness surrounding these plans.
sentences.zh: 但这些计划周围总是存在某种模糊性。

sentences.en: It was never entirely clear that the IRS approved of them.
sentences.zh: 国税局（IRS）是否批准它们从来都不是完全清楚的。

sentences.en: It was never entirely clear that the IRS would continue to approve of them.
sentences.zh: 国税局是否会继续批准它们也从来不是完全清楚的。

sentences.en: And in 1978,
Congress stepped into this vacuum when it passed a broad piece of legislation that included a short provision called Section 401k that attempted to provide greater clarity
sentences.zh: 国会介入了这个真空，通过了一项广泛的立法，其中包含一个名为第401(k)条的简短条款，试图提供更大的清晰度

sentences.en: to how these profit-sharing schemes could be established.
sentences.zh: 关于如何建立这些利润分享计划。

sentences.en: And the people who wrote the legislation didn't think that Section 401k was significant at all.
sentences.zh: 编写这项立法的人根本不认为第401(k)条有什么重要意义。

sentences.en: They thought it was just a sort of inconsequential tweak.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这只是一种无关紧要的微调。

sentences.en: However, a retirement benefits specialist in suburban Philadelphia thought otherwise.
sentences.zh: 然而，费城郊区的一位退休福利专家却有不同的想法。

sentences.en: In 1979, a gentleman named Ted Benna, he had been asked by a local bank to try to devise a profit-sharing program that it could offer to executives.
sentences.zh: 1979年，一位名叫特德·贝纳（Ted Benna）的绅士，被当地一家银行要求尝试设计一个可以提供给高管的利润分享计划。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, in other words, they were doing that same old thing of trying to figure out how to shield the taxes of highly-paid executives.
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，他们正在做那种老旧的事情，试图弄清楚如何为高薪高管避税。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, there he was sitting in his office on a weekend afternoon in 1979 and he started reading quite closely this Section 401k and the light bulb went off.
sentences.zh: 所以，1979年一个周末的下午，他坐在办公室里，开始非常仔细地阅读这个第401(k)条，灵光一闪。

sentences.en: He realized that there was possibly a way to preserve this sort of system legally.
sentences.zh: 他意识到可能有一种方法可以合法地保留这种系统。

sentences.en: Instead of the company making payments directly into these accounts, you could offer them as retirement plans that employees could pay into themselves.
sentences.zh: 与其由公司直接向这些账户付款，不如将它们作为员工可以自己出资的退休计划来提供。

sentences.en: The thinking was that if you paid executives big bonuses, they could choose to put that money into the plan pre-tax.
sentences.zh: 当时的设想是，如果你向高管支付巨额奖金，他们可以选择税前将钱存入该计划。

sentences.en: And he sort of realized he was onto something quite big.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上意识到自己有了重大发现。

sentences.en: The catch was
sentences.zh: 问题在于

sentences.en: Section 401k indicated that this plan had to be made available to rank and file employees at a company.
sentences.zh: 第401(k)条指出，该计划必须向公司的普通员工开放。

sentences.en: And that struck Benna as a challenge because it was one thing for a highly-paid executive to be willing to put aside some of his income in such a way.
sentences.zh: 这让贝纳觉得是一个挑战，因为高薪高管愿意以这种方式存起一部分收入是一回事。

sentences.en: But to ask a bank teller, people who tended to need the money more immediately, that was going to be a big ask.
sentences.zh: 但是要求银行出纳员——那些往往更急需这笔钱的人——这样做，那将是一个巨大的要求。

sentences.en: And solving that piece of the puzzle was a big challenge.
sentences.zh: 而解决这个拼图的那一部分是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: And so what was his solution?
sentences.zh: 那么他的解决方案是什么？

sentences.en: His solution, and it was an ingenious one, was that the bank could offer to match a portion of the contribution that an employee made.
sentences.zh: 他的解决方案——这是一个绝妙的方案——是银行可以提供匹配员工所做贡献的一部分。

sentences.en: So instantly would grow their money.
sentences.zh: 所以会瞬间让他们的钱增长。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's kind of a free money quality to that proposal.
sentences.zh: 这个提议有一种免费送钱的性质。

sentences.en: and that this was the sweetener that could get rank and file employees to go along with it.
sentences.zh: 这就是可以让普通员工随之同行的甜头。

sentences.en: And in that moment, in that flash of inspiration,
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，在灵感闪现的那一刻，

sentences.en: Ted Benna created the modern 401k, which would go on to change the American economic retirement system.
sentences.zh: 特德·贝纳创造了现代401(k)，它将继续改变美国的经济退休系统。

sentences.en: A funny footnote to this is that the bank that had asked
sentences.zh: 关于这一点的一个有趣的花絮是，曾要求

sentences.en: Benna to come up with the plan rejected the plan.
sentences.zh: 贝纳想出这个计划的银行拒绝了这个计划。

sentences.en: It was concerned that the IRS would ultimately rule the scheme illegal.
sentences.zh: 它担心国税局最终会裁定该计划违法。

sentences.en: But Benna was undeterred and decided that he would offer the plan to his own company.
sentences.zh: 但贝纳并没有被吓退，决定将这个计划提供给自己公司的员工。

sentences.en: Benna's colleagues and employees loved the plan and happily contributed to it.
sentences.zh: 贝纳的同事和员工非常喜欢这个计划，并乐意为之出资。

sentences.en: And through word of mouth and articles in local newspapers, the idea took hold.
sentences.zh: 通过口碑和当地报纸上的文章，这个想法流行起来了。

sentences.en: And the timing turned out to be very fortuitous.
sentences.zh: 而时机证明是非常幸运的。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Well, for a couple reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，出于几个原因。

sentences.en: One, a lot of corporations had come to regard pensions as albatrosses.
sentences.zh: 第一，许多公司已经开始将养老金视为累赘。

sentences.en: Certainly in two industries that were best known for their pension programs, auto and steel, these were industries that were in decline and their pension obligations were killing
sentences.zh: 在最以其养老金计划闻名的两个行业，汽车和钢铁，这些行业正在衰退，他们的养老金债务正在杀死

sentences.en: them.
sentences.zh: 他们。

sentences.en: Right, because as you told us earlier, they literally guarantee a certain level of retirement.
sentences.zh: 对，因为正如你之前告诉我们的，它们字面上保证了一定水平的退休生活。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And meeting those guarantees had become increasingly onerous and particularly for companies that were in dying or fading industries.
sentences.zh: 兑现这些保证变得越来越繁重，特别是对于那些处于垂死或衰落行业的公司而言。

sentences.en: And so you have companies looking to get away from this pension system.
sentences.zh: 因此，你看到公司希望摆脱这个养老金系统。

sentences.en: And the politics of that era was also a significant factor.
sentences.zh: 那个时代的政治也是一个重要因素。

sentences.en: I mean, this was when
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是当

sentences.en: Ronald Reagan is president and
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根担任总统并且

sentences.en: Reaganomics, as it was called, was centered around the idea of individual responsibility, individual economic empowerment, and 401ks shifted responsibility for retirement saving
sentences.zh: 里根经济学（正如它被称为的那样）围绕着个人责任、个人经济赋权的理念，而401(k)将退休储蓄的责任从雇主转移到了雇员身上。

sentences.en: from the employer to the employee.
sentences.zh: 真正取决于雇员自己去弄清楚他或她希望钱如何投资。
